Subject: CityBank continuity preflight: warm-start proof & RTO/RPO artifacts

Hi David / Marissa,

Thanks for partnering on CityBank's continuity review. The audit team requested a small, focused packet for our operational preflight before the scheduled witness on Friday. Can you provide the following by end-of-day Thursday (2026-08-27) if possible:  

1) RTO / RPO attestation matrix (current production SLA numbers and whether any exceptions exist) — one page preferred.
2) Recent warm-start logs or a warm-start summary demonstrating a successful service warm-up from snapshot (prefer last three runs).
3) Extract from the runbook that shows the failover sequence we should expect during a warm failover (step numbers, owner roles, estimated operator time).
4) A short list of cross-region dependencies (e.g., KV cache priming, database read replicas) and the mitigations you use.

We may ask for a live witness of a warm-start replay; tentative window is Fri 2026-08-27 10:00–11:30 PT. Can you confirm availability?

If there are any sensitive artifacts that should go to docs@citybank.com via SFTP or a secure Share, flag them in your reply.

Appreciate the quick turn — this is primarily for the SIG/BCP pack.

Best,
Amelia Zhao
Senior BCP Analyst
CityBank — Operational Resilience

--
Amelia Zhao
Amelia.Zhao@citybank.com
From: david_kim@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CityBank continuity preflight: warm-start proof & RTO/RPO artifacts

Amelia — thanks for the clear list. We can get everything over to you and are available for the proposed witness window on Friday 10:00 PT. Below is a concise packet summary; the attached artifacts are the ones you asked for.

Attachments (attached to this message):
- redwood-runbook-v2.1.pdf (excerpted: sections 4.2–4.6 contain warm failover steps and RACI)
- cb-2026-warmstart-log-summary.pdf (last three warm-starts: 2026-06-30, 2026-07-22, 2026-08-10)

Quick RTO / RPO attestation (production, multi-AZ):
- RTO (service availability after warm-start initiation): 8 minutes (target SLA 15 minutes).
- RPO (maximum permitted data loss): 30 seconds for customer write path (replication + WAL shipping).
- Exceptions: none currently. Any scheduled maintenance windows are excluded per contract.

Runbook excerpt (high-level):
1) Trigger detection & page on-call (automated and manual triggers). Owner: Oncall-Infra (Ops).
2) Initiate warm-start orchestration (restore from snapshot, start model-serving containers, restore KV cache warm segment). Owner: Ops Runbook Lead. Estimated duration: 4–7 minutes for base restore, cache priming + model weights ~3–5 minutes depending on sequence length.
3) Health checks and traffic ramp (health probes -> gradual traffic shift -> monitor latency/OPS metrics). Owner: SRE.
4) Rollback path & escalation notes. Owner: Incident Commander.

Cross-region dependencies:
- KV cache priming: we use prefix warming with KV snapshots stored in S3 replicated across regions. Mitigation: staggered priming + fallback to cold-cache with degraded latency.
- DB replicas: asynchronous replicas with WAL replay; mitigation: read-only fallback and throttled write buffer.

If you want, Neha can attach the SIG artifact checklist and a one-page trace of our last warm-start run. We flagged any sensitive logs and will deliver them to docs@citybank.com via scp if you prefer.

Confirming: Fri 2026-08-27 10:00–10:45 PT for a warm-start witness. We'll plan a 30–45 minute session: run through a warm-start replay, review logs, and answer questions.

Thanks —
David Kim
Director, Reliability
Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

Amelia — adding a couple of technical clarifications to David's note so your auditors have precise callouts for the SIG questionnaire:  

- Warm-start logs (attached summary) include a perf trace showing cache hit rate progression (t=0 to t=600s). For SIG/CAIQ please reference the timestamps in the PDF: the warm-start completes to 95% capacity priming within ~180s, and steady-state hit-rate is typically achieved by ~420s under synthetic traffic.

- The RTO figure David listed (8 minutes) is the mean observed across four in-situ warm-starts; our SLA commitment is 15 minutes and we have never exceeded it in production for the last 12 months. We include the test vector IDs in the attached log summary for audit reproducibility.

- Runbook detail: section 4.3 contains the exact CLI command sequence we run during the warm-start (safe to share), section 4.5 lists the prime-cache policy (prefix families and TTLs). We redacted internal hostnames in the attached runbook excerpt.

I also attached a one-page SIG checklist (not full SIG form) that maps your requested artifacts to typical SIG questions (e.g., DR-2: restore verification -> cb-2026-warmstart-log-summary.pdf). If you want the full CAIQ export we can produce it, but that will take an extra business day.
